cards.explanation: The answer is False. A land animal needs both the split hoof and the cud. The camel chews the cud, but the text says it “…does not have a divided hoof; it is unclean for you.” (Leviticus 11:4) So one sign alone doesn't make the cut, friends.

The answers are cud and unclean. The pig has the split hoof, completely divided, but it doesn't chew the cud. The verse says the pig “…does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you.” (Leviticus 11:7) Two signs are required, and the pig brings one. I know, a pig with half the signs feels like it should get partial credit, friends, but the text doesn't give it.

The answer is True. God says, “You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses; they are unclean for you.” (Leviticus 11:8) So the command covers touching the carcasses as well as eating the meat. Keep that in your pocket, bakers, because the passage comes back to touching carcasses later.
The answer is fins and scales. The verse says they may eat "…anything with fins and scales." That goes for the seas and for the streams. A water creature needs both, friends.

The answer is False. Don't eat the meat is one rule. The same verse adds, “…you must detest their carcasses.” (Leviticus 11:11) So there are two parts, friends, and the second one is easy to skim past.

The answer is hopping! The exception is for flying insects “…having jointed legs above their feet for hopping on the ground.” (Leviticus 11:21) Then verse 22 names the kinds: locust, katydid, cricket and grasshopper. So the same bugs I'd swat off my cookie cooling rack are the ones this verse lists as okay to eat. Well, the text says it, friends, not me.

The answer is both kinds: belly crawlers and walkers on four or more feet. The text says, “Do not eat any creature that moves along the ground, whether it crawls on its belly or walks on four or more feet; for such creatures are detestable.” (Leviticus 11:42) Either way, it's covered. Belly or feet, friends, no exceptions in that verse.

The answer is because He is holy. God says, “…consecrate yourselves, therefore, and be holy, because I am holy.” (Leviticus 11:44) The reason He gives is who He is. It's not about the land or anybody else, bakers.

The answer is True. God says, “For I am the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt so that I would be your God…” (Leviticus 11:45) He gives that as His own reason for bringing them out. That's a lot of love packed into one verse about animals, friends.

The answer is clean. The last verse says, “You must distinguish between the unclean and the clean, between animals that may be eaten and those that may not.” (Leviticus 11:47) That's the whole chapter in one sentence, friends. Clean and unclean, side by side.
